candidate.name: bank index
candidate.meaning: A triple of subsets $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ that indexes each value of the two banks.

judged.note: Use another letter for the scalar (for example c) instead of a, because linear-network and subset-network bind a as the bank index (a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)) and the scalar meaning does not hold there.

candidate.name: subset T
candidate.meaning: A three-element subset of $[h]$ used as a varying coordinate, not the linear map of the earlier page.
candidate.earlier_meaning: A linear map of V into itself, the map whose rank and invertibility are discussed.

judged.note: Use another letter for the linear map (for example L) instead of T, because linear-network and subset-network bind T as a three-element subset of [h]; the linear map is not used under that name on those pages.

candidate.name: subset S
candidate.meaning: A three-element subset of $[h]$ used as the varying target coordinate of an invocation.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The linear map that inverts T, when T is invertible.

judged.note: Do not bind S as a separate letter for the inverse; write the inverse as T^{-1} as the rest of the page does, because linear-network and subset-network bind S as a three-element subset of [h].

candidate.name: vertex
candidate.meaning: A source, gate or sink of the network, at which a frame is attached; here the letter names a vertex, not the triple count of the linear-network page.

judged.note: Use vertex letters that are not vector letters from linear-algebra (for example p and q, so that the frame is D_p and edges run from p to q), since the frame page's v names a vertex and linear-algebra's v names a vector in V.

candidate.name: edge start vertex
candidate.meaning: The vertex at which an edge starts, so that the edge runs from $u$ to $v$; here the letter names a vertex.

judged.note: Use another vertex letter for the edge start (for example p in place of u), because linear-algebra binds u as an arbitrary vector in V and the frame page's u names a vertex.

candidate.name: smaller call total
candidate.meaning: The total number of smaller calls, counted as the sum of the ranks of all edge differences.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The vertex at the end of an edge that starts at r.

judged.note: On subset-network, rename the smaller-call total (for example to $c$ or $\sigma$) so it does not reuse $s$ for the edge end vertex of the Frame page, which subset-network builds on. The frame page's $s$ is a vertex, not a count.

candidate.name: dimension loss
candidate.meaning: The total dimension lost on decreasing edges.
candidate.earlier_meaning: A linear map from $V$ into itself, that is, a map with $L(u+v)=L(u)+L(v)$ and $L(cu)=cL(u)$.

judged.note: On subset-network, rename the dimension loss (for example to $\lambda$ or $D$) so it does not reuse $L$ for the linear map of Linear algebra over a field, which subset-network builds on and which binds $L$ on the page as a linear map. The linear map is the standard use, so the later page changes.
